title: Throwing a stoneware dinner plate
subtitle: Opening and pulling a flat dinner plate from stoneware on the wheel
excerpt: A dinner plate is one of the most demanding wheel forms because it is wide and flat: the clay must be spread outward from the centre without losing evenness or height in the rim. This tutorial covers the opening, widening, and floor-levelling sequence for a 26 cm dinner plate in smooth stoneware.
sourceNotes: Technique synthesised from standard wheel-throwing references and practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat disc fixed to the wheel head so a wide form can be lifted off without distortion
Pressing inward and downward on the clay floor to consolidate it and reduce the risk of cracking in the fired piece
The drying stage where clay holds its shape and can be trimmed without collapsing

content.text: A dinner plate requires 900 g of stoneware. Always throw plates on a
so the piece can be removed without handling the soft form.
Fix a bat to the wheel head with clay pads. Centre 900 g of stoneware into a low, wide mound rather than a tall cylinder: plates spread outward, so the clay needs to start flat.

Open the centre with three fingers, leaving a 6 mm floor. Widen the opening by pressing outward from the centre while the wheel spins at medium speed. Widen in 3 to 4 slow passes to avoid stretching the clay too fast and cracking the floor.
to the floor after each widening pass. Press the flat of the wooden rib across the floor from centre to edge to consolidate the clay.
Continue widening to a finished diameter of 26 cm. Use the calipers to check the width. The rim should have a slight upward curve of about 10 mm above the floor level to keep food from sliding off.
Use the metal rib held on the floor at a slight angle to smooth and level the floor in one slow pass from centre to rim. This compresses and smooths in one motion.
Shape the rim with two wet fingers: one inside, one outside, pinching gently upward to a consistent height. Needle-trim any uneven lip at the very top.
Leave on the bat to reach
before trimming the foot ring. Plates warp easily during drying: dry under a loose cloth at room temperature, not in a draughty area.

items.problem: Floor cracks radially from centre outward during drying
items.cause: The floor lacked compression; it was spread outward too quickly.
items.fix: At leather-hard, work fresh slip into any crack and compress the floor again firmly by pressing a firm rib across the crack. Dry slowly under cover

items.problem: Rim undulates unevenly around the plate
items.cause: The clay was not centred precisely enough before opening, so different wall thicknesses wobbled as the wheel spun
items.fix: Trim the rim at leather-hard using the needle tool while the plate turns slowly to level it. Take small amounts off at each pass
